A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REG research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, ablations, computational measurements, and representation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds longer-training results, GPU-hour measurements, and ImageNet 512×512 evaluation.

M1.justification: Joint latent/class-token noising, concatenation, selected-layer alignment, velocity prediction, and inference remain unchanged. However, v2 Equation (9) adds a 1/N sum over n while the surrounding text uses n for the fixed alignment layer. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes the alignment objective or is an imprecise reformulation.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix D and Table 11 add actual ImageNet 512×512 generation experiments to the retained 256×256 evaluation. This extends resolution coverage within the same dataset and class-conditional generation task.

E2.justification: Existing 256×256 comparator sets remain unchanged. The new 512×512 comparison explicitly includes an 'ADM-G, ADM-U' row and separate Simple diffusion U-Net and U-ViT-L variants, whereas v1 lists ADM-U and an undifferentiated Simple diffusion entry.

E3.justification: REG training is extended from the previously reported maximum of 2.4M steps/480 epochs to 4M steps/800 epochs. v2 also adds an 80-epoch 512×512 evaluation and GPU-hours as an efficiency measure. Existing 256×256 sampling, sample counts, metrics, and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B/Table 7 examines whether the previously reported convergence-step savings translate into GPU-hour savings at comparable generation quality. The encoder, alignment-depth, loss-weight, entanglement, guidance, and semantic-representation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds FID 1.8 at 4M steps without CFG and 1.36 at 800 epochs with CFG, beyond v1's 2.2 at 2.4M steps and 1.40 at 480 epochs. It also reports 512×512 FID 1.68 at 80 epochs and matched-quality costs of 39 versus 2380 and 77 versus 1800 GPU-hours. These are additional settings and measurements. Table 4 changes the FID percentage from -56.46% to +56.46%, despite retaining the reduction from 7.90 to 3.44.

T1.justification: Equation (9) receives a local formal revision: the single similarity expression becomes an explicit averaged sum, with ambiguous indexing. Section 3.2 also corrects alignment-target dimensions to the foundation encoder's feature dimension. No new theorem or proof is introduced; the flow/SDE and CKNNA derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: joint image-class denoising, improved generation and semantic learning, negligible inference overhead, and 63×/23× convergence acceleration. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Sections 2 and 3.2 refine the criticism of REPA toward its inability to autonomously generate discriminative representations during inference, and replace 'Full utilization' with 'Improved utilization.' The new appendices extend the interpretation to actual training-resource savings and higher-resolution applicability; no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents eight NVIDIA A40 GPUs and training GPU-hours. Appendix D specifies 448×448 DINOv2 inputs and reports 64×64×3 VAE latents for the new resolution experiment. The existing hyperparameter table and code-access URL are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Ledit, Anchor Token Matching, and From Cradle to Cane, while removing World-consistent Video Diffusion with Explicit 3D Modeling. The related-work discussion modestly refines REG's distinction from REPA without substantially changing its research positioning.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in Sections 3.1–3.2, including notation, dimensional explanations, and the REPA comparison. Two appendix sections are inserted, subsequent sections are renumbered, and affiliation/contact information changes. Most narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's schematic is adjusted and its convergence curve extended. New Tables 7 and 11 display training costs and 512×512 results, while existing performance tables gain rows. Appendix tables and sample galleries move with pagination; the sample images themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The GPU-hour comparison directly strengthens the efficiency evidence beyond iteration counts, and the 512×512 experiment provides additional support for scalability. These are useful incremental gains in validation and documentation. They are partly offset by Table 4's introduced percentage-sign error and Equation (9)'s ambiguous indexing, so the overall improvement is limited.
